title: Three kings. One charge. Spain's future decided in a single day.

beats.text: Three kings. One charge. Spain's future decided in a single day.
In 1195, the Almohads, rulers of Morocco and al-Andalus, crushed King Alfonso the Eighth of Castile at Alarcos.
beats.say: In eleven ninety-five, the Almohads, rulers of Morocco and al-Andalus, crushed King Alfonso the Eighth of Castile at Alarcos.

beats.text: He spent seventeen years preparing his revenge. The Pope proclaimed a crusade.
Castile, Aragon and Navarre marched south together. Legend says a shepherd showed them a hidden path through the mountains.
On the sixteenth of July 1212, they charged the Almohad camp. The caliph's army broke, and the caliph fled.
beats.say: On the sixteenth of July twelve twelve, they charged the Almohad camp. The caliph's army broke, and the caliph fled.

beats.text: A silk banner kept in a monastery in Burgos is said to have been taken that day.
Within forty years, Córdoba and Seville were Christian. Only Granada was left, for two more centuries. Until 1492.
beats.say: Within forty years, Córdoba and Seville were Christian. Only Granada was left, for two more centuries. Until fourteen ninety-two.
